newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iranian patrol boat bumps into U.S. navy ship.
newsitem.headline: Iranian patrol boat bumps into U.S. navy ship.

text.p: An Iranian patrol boat on Sunday bumped into the USS Gettysburg cruiser in the northern Gulf waters, but there were no injuries or serious damage to the U.S. vessel, a U.S. navy spokesman said.

"At noon today (Sunday) the USS Gettysburg was bumped by an Iranian patrol boat, the Bayandor, in the northern Arabian Gulf...There were no injuries on the Gettysburg and only minor damage to some flight deck safety nets on the right side of the ship," Commander T. McCreary told Reuters.
Military sources in the region said the incident did not appear to be intentional on the part of the Iranian boat.

"It does not appear to be intentional and is most probably (poor) shiphandling or equipment error on the Iranian vessel," one source said. The source said it appeared the vessels were on parallel courses.

McCreary said the Gettysburg, with 300 crew members on board, was at the time of the incident escorting the USS Enterprise aircraft carrier on routine flight operations in the Gulf in support of operation Southern Watch over Iraq.
"The Gettysburg and Enterprise remain on station conducting flight operations in support of operation Southern Watch," he said.
"The Bayandor stopped immediately after the incident, but eventually got underway and proceeded away from the Enterprise and Gettysburg," McCreary said.
"An investigation will be conducted into the cause of the incident," he added.
The Enterprise and Gettysburg are part of the U.S. Fifth Fleet, whose area of operations extends from the Red Sea and Horn of Africa in the west to Pakistan in the east.

The Enterprise was moved to the Gulf in September in a U.S. military buildup in the region after Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's forces supported one Kurdish militia group against another in northern Iraq.

Iran has repeatedly said it was opposed to the U.S. presence in the Gulf, saying American warships, part of a multinational force enforcing U.N. sanctions on Iraq for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait, threatened security in the region.
In June this year, it accused the U.S. vessels of violating its sovereignty by harassing its ships in the Gulf waters. The United States denied the charges.
Washington, whose forces in the Gulf keep a close watch on Iran's military moves, accuses the Islamic republic of supporting terrorism and trying to develop nuclear weapons. Iran denies both charges.
